issues.display_title: Issue #171: [20260630] Fix curved-wall persistence, map rendering, and handle-drag sync
issues.main_description_html:
Fix curved-wall persistence, map rendering, and handle-drag sync

Feature-ID: N/A (bugfix on curved-wall feature)
Task: Bugfix
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
Difficulty: Medium
Story Points: N/A
Scheduled: 2026-06-30
Sprint: N/A

Description

Curved walls (bezier-handle drawing) rendered correctly in the 2D editor and three.js 3D view, but two integration bugs surfaced after the feature landed:

  1. Map + persistence layer never carried curve data. WallLayer (the store/persisted wall shape) had no curve fields, so bridge.ts's levelToModel/modelToLevel dropped h1x/h1y/h2x/h2y on every round-trip — refreshing the page flattened curves back to straight walls. The map's canvasDataToGeoJson also walked wall.points as a straight polyline, so curved walls rendered straight on the map even mid-session.
  2. Handle drag/visibility bugs in the editor. Dragging a curved wall's body translated only x1/y1/x2/y2, leaving the bezier handles behind (curve distorted). Handle dots were also always rendered/hit-testable for every curved wall regardless of selection, instead of only the selected wall.

Fix

  • src/store/useMapStore.ts: WallLayer gains optional h1x/h1y/h2x/h2y.
  • src/lib/newEditor/bridge.ts: levelToModel/modelToLevel carry curve handles both directions.
  • src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts: canvasDataToGeoJson tessellates curved walls (bbox, flat-mode LineString, 3D stacked strips).
  • src/lib/newEditor/editor/interactions.ts: wall-body drag now includes handle point refs.
  • src/lib/newEditor/editor/draw.ts + hittest.ts: handle dots only drawn/hit-tested when the wall is selected.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given a curved wall drawn in the editor, When the page is refreshed, Then the curve persists (no flattening).
  • Given a curved wall, When viewed on the map (flat or 3D stacked mode), Then it renders as a curve, not a straight chord.
  • Given a selected curved wall is dragged by its body, When released, Then the curve shape is preserved (handles move with it).
  • Given a curved wall is not selected, Then its control-handle dots are not drawn and cannot be grabbed.

References

  • Commits: 788b67e, d6c9113

Filed by Claude Code — 2026-06-30

RESULT

Implemented and pushed to development (commits 788b67e, d6c9113).

Files changed:

  • src/store/useMapStore.ts — WallLayer gains optional h1x/h1y/h2x/h2y curve-handle fields.
  • src/lib/newEditor/bridge.ts — levelToModel/modelToLevel carry curve handles both directions across the store round-trip.
  • src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts — canvasDataToGeoJson tessellates curved walls for bbox, flat-mode LineString, and 3D stacked strips.
  • src/lib/newEditor/editor/interactions.ts — wall-body drag now includes the curve-handle point refs so handles move with the wall.
  • src/lib/newEditor/editor/draw.ts / hittest.ts — handle dots only drawn/hit-tested when the wall is selected.
  • src/lib/newEditor/__tests__/bridge.test.ts, src/lib/map/__tests__/curved-wall.test.ts (new) — regression tests for the curve round-trip and map tessellation.

issues.display_title: Issue #140: Persist floorplan state per session + reload via /editor/:session
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Description

The editor Save button only marked state clean in-memory (localStorage autosave). There was no server-side persistence and the editor lived on a static /editor route, so saved work could not be reloaded from a shareable/bookmarkable URL.

Persist the full editor state server-side the same way uploaded floor images are stored (under /tmp/gothru-3d-floormap/{session}/), keyed by the gs_session cookie. Temporary store until a real database/API exists.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Save writes the full editor state (canvasData, floorConfigs, information records, categories, location, etc.) to /tmp/gothru-3d-floormap/{session}/floorplan.json.
  • Editor route is /editor/:gs_session; bare /editor redirects to the session-scoped URL.
  • Loading /editor/:session directly adopts that session into the gs_session cookie and loads its data.
  • On restore, the server file (explicit Save) wins over localStorage autosave; localStorage still used as fallback.
  • Storage keyed by session cookie, mirroring the upload/files routes' validation (^[a-f0-9]{16}$).
  • Exit preview button works (regression fix).

RESULT

Implemented full server-side session persistence + session-scoped editor route.

What was done

  • New src/lib/persistence/wizardState.ts — shared buildPersistedState / hydratePersistedState / getSessionCookie (deduped out of the hook).
  • New src/app/api/floorplan/route.ts — POST writes full-state JSON, GET reads it, stored at /tmp/gothru-3d-floormap/{session}/floorplan.json, keyed by gs_session cookie (same validation as upload/files routes, 20 MB cap).
  • src/components/editor/EditorTopbar.tsx — Save button now POSTs the full state to the server then markSaved; spinner + disabled while in flight.
  • src/hooks/useWizardPersistence.ts — restore prefers the server file over localStorage; accepts a URL session override and adopts it as the cookie.
  • src/app/editor/[session]/page.tsx — dynamic route renders the editor and loads that session's data; bare src/app/editor/page.tsx now server-redirects to /editor/{gs_session} (→ /start if no cookie).
  • src/proxy.ts — adopts the /editor/:session URL segment as the gs_session cookie so a shared/bookmarked link loads its data; still auto-generates a session otherwise.
  • src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx — fixed Exit preview button: the feature-toggle bar's empty 8.5rem left padding overlaid the button and swallowed clicks (pointer-events-none on container, pointer-events-auto on its buttons).

Notes

  • Temporary store keyed by session; swap to DB/API later. Storage is keyed by the cookie session (secure), the URL [session] segment is authoritative for adoption.

Typecheck + lint clean.

issues.display_title: Issue #139: Hallways & Open-to-Below: non-interactive white transition space (no hover/click/label)

Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Context

Hallways and Open-to-Below areas are transition space, not points of interest. In the 3D Map tab and the Preview overlay they were rendered like normal rooms — cream floor, hoverable, clickable, with a name label. They should instead read as passive background.

Goal

Make hallway and open-to-below areas non-interactive and visually quiet in both the editor's 3D Map tab and the Preview overlay.

Scope

  • Expose each area's type as an areaType property in the floor-plan GeoJSON.
  • Hallway fill = white (#ffffff) instead of cream (both the 3D extrusion and the flat-mode area fill). Open-to-below keeps its no-slab behaviour.
  • No hover highlight on hallway areas (Map tab + Preview).
  • No click / selection on hallway areas (Map tab + Preview).

  • Rooms are unaffected; selection of real rooms still works.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Setting an area to Hallway turns its floor white in Map + Preview.
  • Hovering a hallway shows no highlight; the cursor stays default.
  • Clicking a hallway does not select it.
  • Hallway and Open-to-Below areas show no name label in Map + Preview.
  • Rooms keep their fill, hover highlight, selection, and label.
  • Typecheck + ESLint pass with zero new errors.

RESULT

Implemented hallway/open-to-below as non-interactive white transition space in the 3D Map tab and Preview.

  • Exposed areaType on GeoJSON area features (geojson-utils.ts).
  • Hallway fill = #ffffff via a data-driven match on areaType, in both the 3D extrusion paint and the flat-mode area fill (layer-definitions.ts). Open-to-below keeps no slab.
  • Hover highlight skipped for hallway: Editor3DMapView + PreviewOverlay mousemove handlers early-return on areaType === "hallway".
  • Selection skipped for hallway: useMapSelect feature-click + PreviewOverlay click handlers early-return.
  • Name labels suppressed for hallway and open-to-below: the 3D label-canvas anchor build (useFloorPlanLabels.ts) skips them, and the flat-mode area-label symbol layer filters them out.

Rooms unaffected (fill, hover, selection, label intact). Verified the GeoJSON emits areaType (room/hallway) via a direct unit harness.

issues.display_title: Issue #138: Search and Directions in Preview
issues.main_description_html:
Search and Directions in Preview

Docs

Spec

2026-06-22-search-direction-area-design.md

Plan

2026-06-22-search-direction-area.md

Context

All the pieces now exist — the route-finding engine, the shared search box, the Search panel, and the Directions panel. This final task connects them inside preview mode so visitors can actually use them on the map.

Goal

Bring Search Area and Directions into preview mode: add the toggle to switch between them, enforce the single-floor rule, draw the route and markers on the map, handle tapping to drop a starting pin, and add a "Directions" shortcut to the information card.

What We're Building

The full integration in preview mode:

  • Two toggle buttons (Search Area and Directions) that are mutually exclusive — turning one on turns the other off, and clicking the active one turns it off.
  • The panels in the top-right — the Search panel or the Directions panel appears when its mode is active.
  • A single-floor rule — if more than one floor is shown at once, each feature is replaced by a short notice that it only works with a single active floor. Only areas on the active floor ever appear in results.
  • Search behaviour — choosing a search result pans and focuses the map on that area and opens its information card.
  • Directions behaviour:
    • Blue dots drawn at the centre of every area that has information, marking the valid endpoints.
    • A blue route line drawn between the start and the destination, routed around walls and through doorways by the engine from the first task.
    • In Drop Pin mode, tapping the map places (or moves) a starting pin, and the route is drawn from that pin.
    • A "Directions" button on the information card, so the visitor can set the area they're currently viewing as the destination.
  • No-route handling — when a start and destination can't be connected, the "No route available" message is shown instead of a line.

Why It Matters

This is where the feature becomes real for visitors. It also gathers all the fiddly map-and-state coordination into one place, built on top of pieces that were each proven on their own — which is exactly what keeps this large step manageable.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Only one of Search or Directions can be active at a time.
  • With more than one floor visible, both features show the single-floor notice and hide their inputs; results only ever include active-floor areas.
  • Selecting a search result focuses the map on that area and shows its information.
  • Blue endpoint dots appear for areas with information while Directions is active.
  • A blue, wall-avoiding route line is drawn for both starting modes (a chosen area or a dropped pin); "No route available" shows when there is no path.
  • Tapping the map in Drop Pin mode sets the starting point; the information card's "Directions" button sets the destination.
  • The codebase builds, typechecks, and lints with zero new errors.
  • The change is committed on its own.

What Changes After This Task

Visitors can search for an area or get a wall-aware route between two points directly in preview mode — the feature is complete.

RESULT

Wired Search Area + Directions into PreviewOverlay: mutually-exclusive toggle, top-right panels, single-floor rule (results limited to the active floor; notice when >1 floor), blue wall-aware route line + endpoint dots, drop-pin placement, and a "Directions" button on the info card. Search focuses the map + opens the info card. Route is computed via the Task 1 pathfinder and converted to lng/lat.

Also added a developer-only routing nav-grid debug overlay (red=wall, orange=room, green=corridor), gated behind a dev_mode cookie set by middleware when the x-developer-mode header matches DEVELOPER_MODE_CODE (.env.example documents it).

issues.display_title: Issue #134: Wall-Aware Route Finding
issues.main_description_html:
Wall-Aware Route Finding

Docs

Spec

2026-06-22-search-direction-area-design.md

Plan

2026-06-22-search-direction-area.md

Context

Preview mode lets a visitor look at a floor, but there is no way to work out how to walk from one spot to another. Before any on-screen "Directions" feature can draw a path, the app needs a brain that can figure out a sensible walking route — one that goes around walls and through doorways, just like a person would.

This task builds that brain only. Nothing appears on screen yet.

Goal

Create the route-finding engine: a self-contained piece of logic that, given a starting point and a destination on a single floor, returns the shortest walking route that never cuts through a wall — or clearly reports that no route is possible.

What We're Building

A standalone routing module that:

  • Reads the floor's walls and doorways.
  • Lays an invisible fine grid over the floor and marks each little square as either blocked (a wall) or open. Doorways are treated as open, so routes can pass through them.
  • Finds the shortest open path from start to finish, going around buildings and obstacles and through doors as needed.
  • Tidies the result into a clean set of turning points instead of hundreds of tiny steps.
  • Returns a clear "no route" answer when the destination is walled off with no way in.
  • Still finds a route even if the start or end happens to land right on a wall, by snapping to the nearest open spot.

Why It Matters

Routing is the hardest and most reusable part of the Directions feature. Building it on its own — with no buttons or map drawing involved — means it can be trusted before anything visual is layered on top. Both ways a visitor can start a route (picking an area or dropping a pin) will rely on this exact same engine.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given a start and a destination on one floor, it returns a path that stays out of walls and uses doorways.
  • When the destination is fully enclosed with no opening, it clearly reports that no route exists.
  • A start or end point sitting on a wall still produces a route by snapping to the nearest open spot.
  • The codebase builds and typechecks with zero new errors.
  • The change is committed on its own so the routing engine is independently traceable.

What Changes After This Task

The route-finding engine exists and is ready for the Directions panel to call once the visitor has chosen a start and a destination.

RESULT

Wall-aware route finding implemented as a pure module src/lib/routing/pathfinder.ts (no DOM, testable): computeLevelBbox, buildGrid, findPath. Grid A* in canvas-pixel space — walls rasterized as thick blocked lines, doorways carved back open, 8-directional search with a binary min-heap, endpoint snap-to-nearest-open, collinear simplification; returns a simplified pixel path or null when no route exists.

Tuned extensively against a real floor plan:

  • Navigable space limited to the building interior (areas) so routes can't wander outside.
  • Wall half-width floored at one cell so thin walls reliably block.
  • Doorways carved as a tight capsule along the door segment (not an axis-aligned box) so an opening never bridges rooms that lack a door.
  • No diagonal corner-cutting.
  • A clearance field (Chamfer distance transform) centres routes in corridors and through door middles, capped so wide-open/exterior space isn't preferred over a bounded corridor.
  • Soft room penalty so routes favour corridors where one connects.

Feature-ID: 202606170000-GoThru_3D_Floormap-Editor_Tools_Improvement
Task: T-24
Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Sprint: Editor Tools Improvement

Description

Area labels in the Map (3D) tab were HTML DOM overlays recomputed every render frame, causing lag with many labels and flicker. MapLibre symbol layers cannot be elevated onto a fill-extrusion, so to seat each label on its own level's floor height (Mappedin-style) the labels are now drawn on a single 2D canvas overlay via a MapLibre custom layer. The custom layer provides the world→clip matrix (defaultProjectionData.mainMatrix) each frame; each label's ground centroid is lifted to its level floor altitude with MercatorCoordinate.fromLngLat([lng,lat], h) and projected, then drawn with fillText plus a greedy declutter pass. No DOM nodes, no per-frame React, no GeoJSON setData churn.

Dependencies

Editor tools improvement spec; existing 3D map view (Editor3DMapView)

Acceptance Criteria

  • Given multiple area labels in the Map tab, When the user pans/zooms/pitches/rotates, Then labels stay smooth (no DOM/React per frame) and do not flicker.
  • Given a multi-level building, When a label belongs to level N, Then it appears at level N's floor height and rises/falls correctly with camera pitch.
  • Given overlapping labels, When rendered, Then a greedy declutter hides colliding labels.
  • Given "Show labels" is toggled off, Then no labels are drawn.

References

  • Spec: §5 AREA (labels), Map rendering
  • Technique: MapLibre custom layer + MercatorCoordinate altitude (as used by Mappedin)
  • Files: src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLabels.ts, src/components/editor/Editor3DMapView.tsx

RESULT

Replaced the per-frame HTML/React label overlay with a single 2D canvas overlay driven by a MapLibre custom layer. Each frame the layer supplies defaultProjectionData.mainMatrix; per-area ground centroids are lifted to their level floor altitude via MercatorCoordinate.fromLngLat([lng,lat], baseH), projected to screen, and drawn with fillText + halo, plus a greedy declutter pass and behind-camera/off-screen culling. True floor-height elevation (level N at level-N floor), no DOM nodes, no symbol-layer flicker.
